method.primary: faster-whisper 1.2.1; Systran/faster-whisper-small.en; CPU int8; word_timestamps=True; supplied script used only as initial_prompt; no forced decoding
method.verification: Independent unprompted full recording and unprompted 54.0 s-to-end crop using the same local small.en model.
method.repaired_asr_error: The primary prompted pass dropped Congress and no at a decoder segment boundary and assigned Tell an implausible 20 ms duration. The complete Tell Congress no ... safe span was replaced with unprompted crop timings, verified independently by the unprompted full pass.
method.timing_precision_note: Model-derived word boundaries, normally on a 20 ms grid; allow roughly 0.1–0.2 s perceptual tolerance. These are not manually verified phoneme alignments.
method.probability_note: Whisper token probabilities are diagnostic only, not calibrated probabilities of correct transcription. Emphasized uppercase words such as TODAY have low probabilities in the prompted pass despite independent lexical agreement.
method.caption_note: Captions retain the supplied script wording, punctuation, and emphasis after word-level content agreement; timing follows the actual recording. End times include up to 0.20 s reading hold or minimum 0.90 s cue where space permits, with no overlap.
method.scene_note: Suggested scene boundaries fall halfway through inter-beat voice gaps, rounded frame values are also provided. Editorial transitions can overlap these boundaries.

beats.text: The richest companies on Earth are racing to build AI that can do your job. MY job. EVERY job.
They call it superintelligence. Let's call it what it is: human-replacement AI.
The plan: build something smarter than all of us. The problem: nobody knows how to control it. Not even its makers.
This July, OpenAI tested more than a thousand AI agents that were supposed to be isolated.
and seven hundred of them hacked Hugging Face, a major AI platform.
Nobody programmed them to do that.
And they tried to fake their logs to cover their tracks.
This is TODAY'S AI. Next time, it won't be a test.
All the AI companies are racing to be first. They aren't worried about the guardrails.
Benjamin Franklin played with lightning, then built something to keep it from burning Philly down.
The tech companies don't care what they burn down.
Join PhillyPause. Share this video. Tell Congress: no superintelligence until we know it will be safe.
Franklin built a lightning rod. This time, it's us.
